question: A woman presenting with homogeneous grey-white vaginal discharge, positive whiff test, and clue cells on wet mount should be treated with oral fluconazole 150 mg as a single dose.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually false. Clue cells, positive whiff test, and grey-white discharge are diagnostic of bacterial vaginosis (BV). BV is caused by anaerobic bacteria (Gardnerella, Mobiluncus), not fungi. Fluconazole is an antifungal used for Candida, not BV. Prescribing antifungals for BV is the commonest management error — review the treatment section.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. The described findings (grey-white discharge, positive whiff test, clue cells) are diagnostic of bacterial vaginosis, NOT vulvovaginal candidiasis. BV requires metronidazole (400–500 mg orally twice daily for 7 days or 2 g single dose), not antifungals. Fluconazole is for candidiasis (white curdy discharge, pruritus, no fishy odour).
